correctness.rationale: Distance four makes every two-coordinate projection injective, so a hypothetical size-16 code would project bijectively onto all 16 ordered symbol pairs for each of ten coordinate pairs. That forces 40 equal-coordinate incidences. But a length-five word of symbol weight at most two has composition \((2,2,1,0)\) or \((2,1,1,1)\), contributing at most two equal-coordinate pairs, so 16 words contribute at most 32, contradiction. The displayed 15-word witness was independently checked for symbol weight and all pairwise distances. At size 15 each projection misses one pair and therefore contains at least three diagonals, yielding at least 30 equal-coordinate incidences; the per-word upper bound is also 30, forcing every word to type \((2,2,1,0)\) and each missing pair to be diagonal. A fresh independent witness/projection replay confirmed all ten projections.

value.rationale: This is a natural smallest boundary where the unrestricted Singleton size 16 is ruled out specifically by the symbol-multiplicity constraint, and the exact one-word deficit comes with a complete forced local projection structure for every optimum. That makes the finite result a useful benchmark for symbol-weight packing/design theory rather than a bare brute-force datum.
residual_risks: The theorem does not reveal a general family beyond this boundary case.

final_claim: The largest quaternary length-five code of symbol weight two and Hamming distance at least four has size \(15\); moreover every maximum code consists entirely of composition type \((2,2,1,0)\), and every two-coordinate projection contains 15 distinct ordered pairs and omits exactly one diagonal pair.
limitations: No equivalence classification or enumeration of all maximum codes.
